text: Now Jericho was shut up tight because of the Israelites. No one went out, and no one came in.
And the LORD said to Joshua, "See, I have delivered Jericho into your hand, along with its king and its fighting men.
March around the city with all your soldiers, circling it once. Do this for six days.
Seven priests shall carry seven ram's-horn trumpets before the ark. On the seventh day march around the city seven times, with the priests blowing the trumpets.

When they sound a long blast on the ram's horn and you hear the trumpet, all the people are to give a great shout. Then the city wall will collapse, and the people shall charge straight in, each man where he stands."

versions.text: When they sound a long blast on the ram's horn and you hear the trumpet, all the people are to give a great shout. Then the city wall will collapse, and the people shall charge straight in, each man ahead of him."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew phrase 'ish negdo' means 'each man straight before him' — i.e., each man advances at the point opposite where he is standing. 'Each man ahead of him' is confusing English (the pronoun has no clear referent) and reads as if the men are ahead of someone else. It is also redundant beside 'charge straight in.'

text: So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven ram's-horn trumpets before the ark of the LORD."
And he said to the people, "Move out and march around the city, and let the armed men go ahead of the ark of the LORD."

When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven ram's-horn trumpets before the LORD moved forward, blowing the trumpets, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed behind them.
The armed men marched ahead of the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard followed the ark, while the trumpets sounded on and on.
But Joshua had commanded the people, "Do not shout, do not let your voice be heard, do not let a single word leave your mouth until the day I tell you to shout. Then shout!"
So he had the ark of the LORD carried around the city, circling it once. Then they returned to the camp and spent the night there.
Joshua rose early the next morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.

The seven priests carrying the seven ram's-horn trumpets before the ark of the LORD went on, blowing the trumpets as they marched. The armed men went ahead of them, and the rear guard followed the ark of the LORD, while the trumpets sounded on and on.
On the second day they marched around the city once and returned to the camp. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day they rose at daybreak and marched around the city in the same way, seven times. Only on that day did they circle the city seven times.

versions.text: On the seventh day they rose at daybreak and marched around the city in the same way, but seven times. That day alone they circled the city seven times.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew emphasis is 'only on that day' (raq bayyom hahu). 'But seven times' followed by 'That day alone' reads as clumsy duplication when spoken aloud; the revision keeps the Hebrew emphasis while flowing better.

text: On the seventh time around, when the priests sounded the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, "Shout! For the LORD has given you the city.
The city and everything in it are devoted to the LORD for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, she and all who are with her in her house, because she hid the messengers we sent.
But keep away from what is devoted to destruction, or you will bring destruction on yourselves by taking any of it. You would make the camp of Israel liable to destruction and bring disaster upon it.
All the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron are holy to the LORD; they must go into the LORD's treasury."

So the people shouted, and the trumpets sounded. When the people heard the blast of the trumpet, they raised a great shout, and the wall fell down flat. The people charged into the city, each man where he stood, and they captured it.

versions.text: So the people shouted, and the trumpets sounded. When the people heard the blast of the trumpet, they raised a great shout, and the wall collapsed. The people charged straight into the city, each man ahead of him, and they captured it.
versions.explanation: Same issue as verse 5: 'each man ahead of him' is unclear English for 'ish negdo' ('each straight before him'). The correction also removes the redundancy with 'charged straight into.'

versions.text: So the people shouted, and the trumpets sounded. When the people heard the blast of the trumpet, they raised a great shout, and the wall collapsed. The people charged into the city, each man where he stood, and they captured it.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew adds tachteha, 'under it / in its place,' stressing that the wall dropped flat where it stood rather than merely giving way. 'Fell down flat' captures this without lengthening the line, and the strong monosyllables read well aloud.

text: They devoted to destruction everything in the city, putting to the sword man and woman, young and old, ox, sheep, and donkey.
To the two men who had scouted the land Joshua said, "Go into the prostitute's house and bring her out, along with everyone belonging to her, as you swore to her."

So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father and mother, her brothers, and everyone belonging to her. They brought out her whole family and left them outside the camp of Israel.

versions.text: So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father and mother, her brothers, and everyone belonging to her. They brought out her whole family and settled them outside the camp of Israel.
versions.explanation: The verb 'yannichum' means 'they set/left them,' a temporary placement outside the camp (as ritually unclean outsiders). 'Settled' wrongly implies permanent residence, which is only later described in verse 25.

text: Then they burned the city and everything in it, but the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron they placed in the treasury of the LORD's house.
Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her father's household, and all who belonged to her, and she has lived among Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers Joshua had sent to spy out Jericho.

At that time Joshua pronounced this oath: "Cursed before the LORD is the man who undertakes to rebuild this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundation; at the cost of his youngest he will set up its gates."
So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the land.
